zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue describes a spatial relationship, enforce the correct positional constraint: use inequality for ordering and adjacency for immediate neighbors.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions relative positions such as 'next to', 'to the left of', 'to the right of', 'somewhere left of', or 'somewhere right of'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'next to' as 'somewhere left of' (allowing any distance) or treating 'somewhere left of' as 'immediately left of'.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that exactly N houses separate them, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue specifies a numeric distance between two items.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting '2 houses between X and Y' as X and Y being exactly 2 houses apart, rather than having 2 houses in between.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values, they must belong to the same house; propagate this binding throughout the puzzle.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue states that two attributes refer to the same person (e.g., 'the person who loves pop music is the person who loves romance books').
zebralogic.example: Assigning pop music to one house and romance books to a different house despite the clue linking them.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only a strict ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(Y) < pos(X)).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like 'somewhere left of' or 'somewhere right of' without indicating adjacency.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'somewhere left of' as meaning 'immediately left of' and thus restricting positions incorrectly.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house or forbids two attributes from co‑occurring, enforce that prohibition.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue says 'X is not in house Y' or 'X cannot be Y' or similar negative statements.
zebralogic.example: Allowing a value that a clue explicitly forbids to be assigned to a house.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value, remove it from other houses' possibilities.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout solving, whenever a value is placed in a house, eliminate it from the domains of all other houses for that attribute.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same book genre to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final grid, copy each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem state.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the final answer generation step.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'Blue Master' to 'blue master' in the output.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it and propagate.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a domain for a variable reduces to a single option.
zebralogic.example: Failing to assign a value when only one possible house remains, leaving it ambiguous.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate overlapping attribute values using clue context
zebralogic.principle: When a word could belong to more than one attribute category, use surrounding words in the clue to determine the correct category.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a term appears that could be interpreted as multiple attribute types (e.g., a color that is also a cigar name).
zebralogic.example: Misinterpreting 'blue' as a color when the clue refers to the 'Blue Master' cigar.

zebralogic.title: Interpret 'next to each other' as adjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X and Y are next to each other, enforce that they occupy immediately neighboring houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like 'next to', 'adjacent', or 'immediately left/right of'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'next to' as 'somewhere left of' (any distance) instead of requiring adjacency.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrasing and treats the numeric value as the total distance between the two houses, forgetting that the houses themselves occupy the ends.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that there are exactly N houses separating them, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model processes each attribute independently and does not propagate the equality constraint across categories.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attributes, bind them to the same house and propagate this binding throughout the puzzle.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model fails to maintain a global uniqueness constraint, allowing duplicate values in a category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After assigning a value to a house, remove that value from the candidate sets of all other houses for that attribute.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text or applies its own formatting, changing the original representation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement when producing the final answer.
